elements.element: Customer has no obligation to appoint or use Vendor as its sole or exclusive provider.
elements.evidence: Section 2.2 expressly makes Vendor a “non-exclusive provider,” and Section 12.3 confirms that Customer has made no exclusivity commitment and remains free to engage any supplier.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to exclusivity, the exclusivity applies only to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: the operative language imposes no exclusivity on Customer. Section 2.2 is expressly non-exclusive, and Section 12.3 disclaims any exclusivity commitment.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to exclusivity, the exclusivity lasts no more than 12 months.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because Customer has no exclusivity obligation; therefore, no exclusivity period requires a 12-month cap.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to exclusivity, the exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet applicable service levels.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the operative language imposes no exclusivity on Customer, so no exclusivity obligation needs this termination trigger.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to exclusivity, the exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet applicable delivery dates.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the operative language imposes no exclusivity on Customer, so no exclusivity obligation needs this termination trigger.

result.reason: The redline removes the sole-and-exclusive commitment and affirmatively characterizes Vendor as non-exclusive, consistent with the unchanged operative no-exclusivity language in Section 12.3. This fully achieves the preferred position; the fallback is also satisfied because its condition—Customer being subject to exclusivity—is demonstrably absent. The change is narrowly targeted and does not disturb unrelated commercial terms.
